name: Multiculturalism
summary: Multiculturalism holds that a state should recognise and accommodate its cultural, ethnic, linguistic and religious diversity rather than require minorities to assimilate. It combines equal citizenship with group-sensitive measures such as language support, religious accommodation and, for national minorities and indigenous peoples, self-government. Critics argue it undermines cohesion, national identity or gender equality; adherents dispute this.
scope: Liberal multiculturalism as a public philosophy and policy in Western democracies, based on Canadian official policy (the Multiculturalism Act), Will Kymlicka, Charles Taylor and Bhikhu Parekh. It excludes the descriptive sense of mere demographic diversity and radical identity-politics variants, and says little on economic questions.

sources.usedFor: Theoretical positions of Kymlicka, Taylor, Parekh and critics.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Multiculturalism arose as a rejection of assimilation ideals, holding that immigrants may keep their cultural identity while integrating.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Multiculturalism treats cultural plurality within one state as normal and valuable, the opposite of a mono-ethnic national ideal.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Canadian Act pairs recognition of diversity with equal treatment and equal protection under the law for all individuals.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Supporters link multiculturalism to removing barriers that kept minorities from full equality, and the Act promotes removing barriers to participation.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Adherents see the national culture as plural and evolving, and reject privileging one culture; critics say it weakens host culture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Supporters see immigration as socially and economically valuable, with Canada as the model.

open-borders.rationale: Multiculturalism supports immigration and fair integration but is mostly a theory about managing diversity within borders, not about abolishing borders.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Self-government claims are strongest for indigenous peoples and national minorities in the Kymlicka account.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Kymlicka defends group-differentiated rights; Barry, a critic, rejects them as incompatible with universalist liberalism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Defenders argue diversity does not itself undermine cohesion and cite cross-national evidence of no systematic trade-off.

elite-replacement.rationale: Multiculturalists see immigration as legitimate policy; the replacement claim is a critic narrative, not a multicultural position.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Taylor presumes the equal worth of cultures and Parekh argues justice must emerge from dialogue among cultures, though not every adherent denies all comparison.

universal-morality.rationale: Liberal multiculturalists keep universal liberal values as a starting point while Parekh says no framework is impartial; adherents are split.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Parekh and Kymlicka deny state cultural neutrality, but this is not a claim about knowledge in general.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious exemptions from general laws and accommodation are central, so uniform treatment regardless of religion is resisted.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents defend religious accommodation and toleration but do not generally want religion to play a larger role.

separate-church-state.rationale: Accommodating religious practice is central, but adherents mostly accept liberal secular states; split on strictness.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Liberal multiculturalists often favor secular schools while some accommodate faith schools; split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Multiculturalism promotes equal treatment and removal of racial barriers, directly opposing legal segregation.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposed by the commitment to equal worth and to removing barriers to participation of all origins.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressuring minorities to leave contradicts protecting minority communities and their historic contributions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-government is defended for national minorities such as Quebec, though not an independent-state claim.

revive-national-language.rationale: Policies support minority and indigenous languages, e.g. Bolivia and Canada, so revival is broadly favored.

right-to-secede.rationale: Quebec-style autonomy is defended but adherents are split on secession.

harm-principle.rationale: Kymlicka rejects internal restrictions and defends external protections, a liberal harm-style limit.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberal democracy is the setting of the theory.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Recognition and redistribution are both held necessary, but no stance on priority to the poor.

positive-liberty.rationale: Kymlicka justifies group rights by disadvantages that undermine real choice, close to a material view of freedom.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality is valued but religious communities seek accommodation; adherents split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language accommodation is a defining multicultural policy and is written into the Canadian Act.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions are described as central to multicultural policy, though contested by Barry.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Multicultural theorists support minority self-government but not a particular way of rewriting constitutions.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Multiculturalism's accommodation of religious practice and institutions is central, and it opposes state control of churches.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Self-government and distinct institutions for national minorities and indigenous peoples is a core multicultural policy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Multiculturalism is liberal and equal-citizenship based, so a sacred ruler of divine descent is incompatible with it. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Canadian Act and liberal multiculturalism rest on equal citizenship and legal rights for all, so rulers are bound by law. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

land-redistribution.rationale: The scope excludes economic questions; only indigenous land claims touch it, and adherents are not agreed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Kymlicka defends group rights but rejects internal restrictions that deny members basic liberties, including exit.

women-must-cover.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism rejects internal restrictions on group members; head coverings are protected as a free choice, not a duty.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Kymlicka and the Canadian Act support minority self-government and cultural institutions, mainly within the state.

ban-cartels.rationale: The scope excludes economic questions and adherents are not agreed on competition policy.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Multiculturalism rests on equal respect for cultures and rejects ranking societies as more or less advanced, which is the premise of tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Adherents are split: Kymlicka-style liberals support civic nation-building, while others stress plural identities; the sources do not settle schooling.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Act commits government to equal treatment and non-discrimination, and adherents support anti-discrimination law over a right to refuse service.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism protects minority rights through entrenched constitutional guarantees such as the Canadian Charter, which the Act itself invokes.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Says little on economic questions, as the scope notes.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal citizenship is a core principle, so reserving offices for the native-born contradicts it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Kymlicka supports self-government rights for indigenous peoples over their own affairs, not leadership by indigenous descendants over the whole country; equal citizenship leans against the statement.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Adherents are split between preserving history and respecting minorities' objections.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberal multiculturalists such as Kymlicka accommodate cultural diversity within liberal-democratic institutions; the sources do not argue that other civilizations need different political institutions.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not a multicultural issue; the ideology says little on economic questions per its scope.

single-official-language.rationale: Multiculturalism supports minority-language rights and rejects imposing one language on public life, as in the Canadian Act's language provisions.

corporate-influence.rationale: The liberal multiculturalism described here is mainly about cultural recognition and says little on lobbying, so this is a neutral inference.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Multiculturalism Act commits to equal treatment of all cultural communities, which rejects casting a minority as a hostile conspiracy.

religious-nation.rationale: It treats a plural, multi-faith society as the goal and equal status for all religions, which rejects a nation defined by one religion.

religion-illusion.rationale: Multiculturalism treats religion as a legitimate identity to be accommodated, so it rejects the view that religion is mere illusion.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Act supports heritage languages alongside the official ones, and pluralism treats language borrowing and mixing as normal. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-steered settlement to dilute minority regions is the kind of assimilationist nation-building multiculturalism opposes.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism is a liberal-democratic doctrine that protects pluralism and association.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Kymlicka and others support self-government for national minorities and Indigenous peoples, and reject colonial subordination.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Accommodating Muslims and other minorities is central; the claim of incompatibility is what multiculturalism disputes.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious accommodation, including dress, is a defining multicultural measure.

property-franchise.rationale: Equal citizenship regardless of group is central; wealth tests exclude minorities and are rejected by inference from the Act.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Canadian Act affirms equal participation of all individuals regardless of origin, the opposite of an ethnic franchise.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Multiculturalism accommodates religious diversity and holds that groups should not be disadvantaged for their religion. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: It treats religious minorities as equal members of society, opposing discrimination against their businesses. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Multiculturalism Act protects religious freedom and accommodation of religious diversity, which is inconsistent with state-imposed atheism. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents split between equal gender treatment and accommodating religious communities' own practices, a known critique of the doctrine.

rent-control.rationale: Housing economics is outside multiculturalism's scope; adherents split along their wider left or liberal leanings.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Distributive economics is outside the doctrine's scope, and liberal multiculturalists hold varied views.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Multiculturalism rejects the idea of a single homogeneous nation with one ancient lineage, treating plural cultures as part of the nation.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Multiculturalism accommodates religious traditions but is internally split on testing them against gender equality (the Okin debate).

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Equal citizenship and non-discrimination for all groups, as the Canadian Act states, rule out reserving economic life for a majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Kymlicka supports self-government for national minorities but the doctrine does not prescribe merging regions; adherents differ.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Multiculturalism is an equal-citizenship doctrine that opposes racial discrimination and racial supremacy; it recognises cultures, not race-based organising against others.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Multiculturalism rejects defining the nation by one shared language and ethnicity, and treats the state as a framework for several cultural communities.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Multiculturalism accommodates group difference, but the SEP records a feminist dispute over it and adherents are split on gendered group values.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not an issue multiculturalism addresses; adherents are split.

farm-price-support.rationale: Multiculturalism is indifferent to agricultural economic policy.

ban-fgm.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism accommodates cultural practices only within individual rights, so it does not protect harmful practices such as FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism pairs group accommodation with equal citizenship and individual rights, including for women within minority groups.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Adherents are split: Canada's policy supports integration and official languages, while others oppose compulsion.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Multiculturalism holds that religious communities should be accommodated on equal terms, and the Canadian Act affirms equal treatment of all faiths and origins.

women-suffrage.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism rests on equal citizenship, and Kymlicka-style versions limit group rights that violate individual rights such as women's. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

race-social-construct.rationale: The multicultural literature generally treats ethnic and racial identities as socially formed and not biologically fixed. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Liberal multiculturalists such as Kymlicka accept group rights only if individual rights, including women's equality, are protected inside the group; this is the core of the gender-equality debate in the SEP entry.

national-church-status.rationale: The Canadian Multiculturalism Act commits to equality before the law for all regardless of religion or origin, which cuts against a legally privileged national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Self-government and territorial autonomy for national minorities and indigenous peoples is a defining element of Kymlicka's liberal multiculturalism, as the scope states.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Equal citizenship and rights under the Canadian Multiculturalism Act are incompatible with killing without trial.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The doctrine says little on economics; adherents are split between left and liberal strands.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is outside the doctrine and adherents are split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Economic policy is not part of the doctrine and adherents are split between universal and targeted approaches.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Adherents are split between secular neutrality and accommodating religious communities in public life.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Multiculturalism is mainly about cultural recognition and is silent on theories of distributive justice; liberals in the tradition differ.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Multiculturalism has no recorded view on automation or working time.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Multiculturalism combines shared citizenship with cultural recognition and accepts civic patriotism, but it says little on working-class politics; adherents are split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Multiculturalism centres cultural recognition for minorities, so it rejects ranking it behind material interests.

missingStatements.text: Governments should support minority languages in schools, public services and elections.
missingStatements.rationale: Language accommodation is a defining multicultural policy and is written into the Canadian Act.

missingStatements.text: Members of religious minorities should be exempt from general laws that burden their religious practice.
missingStatements.rationale: Religious exemptions are described as central to multicultural policy, though contested by Barry.

notes: Liberal multiculturalists (Kymlicka) reject internal restrictions; Taylor and Parekh are more communitarian or dialogical. Most economic and institutional answers are inferences.
